messages:
anya: Heads-up: saw a KV-cache OOM in prod this morning on a long-context stream (customer A, ~48k tokens). stacktrace points to kv_alloc() while trying to materialize a new slab.
max: Ugh. Any immediate mitigations? Canary or rollback we can do fast?
anya: We disabled canary-specific kernel override and pushed a soft-evict threshold bump to 0.75 -> 0.85 for the affected pool. That stopped the hard OOMs for now but we still saw memory growth across requests.
eli: I ran a quick perf profile on a repro rig. Two interesting things: (1) when kernel-selection picks the fused-attn kernel we allocate a transient scratch buffer (~200MB/request) before streaming starts; (2) KV slabs are being repeatedly split and reallocated due to fragmentation from mixed short+long contexts.
sara: Can you paste the profiler output? Also we should add an automatic fallback policy: if allocation fails once, route that session to the smaller-quantized variant and mark for later analysis.
eli: Perf excerpt (summarized):
```
heap_before: 6.1GB
kv_cache_live: 5.2GB
scratch_peak_per_req: 180MB
heap_after: 11.8GB
Top alloc sites: kv_slab_split(), fused_attn_scratch_alloc(), kv_reuse_try()
```
anya: Repro command I used:
```
# run on repro-node
./run_inference --model redwood-13b-q4 --seed-session --context 48000 --profile kv --trace 1 > /tmp/kvtrace.log
```
anya: /tmp/kvtrace.log attached to the incident ticket: https://redwood-internal/ops/incidents/INC-2026-042 (link)
max: Ok. For immediate protection: (A) add 503 fallback to CPU/quantized route when kv_alloc fails, with exponential backoff; (B) enable aggressive prefix eviction for sessions exceeding 32k tokens; (C) lower fused-attn scratch reservation for long contexts.
sara: I can ship (A) and (B) as a runtime flag. (C) needs kernel-owner signoff but we can gate it behind a rollout.
eli: Also we should consider batching heuristic change: avoid co-scheduling very short and very long contexts into same worker since that increases fragmentation churn. We can add a quick routing rule to keep long-context-only workers isolated.
perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.internal/redwood/kvcache/2026-03-15 - shows correlation between fused_attn kernel selection and jumpy mem spikes. Flamegraphs attached.
ops-bot: Deployed soft-evict bump -> 0.85 at 09:12 UTC, rolled back canary override at 09:25 UTC. No further hard OOMs observed since 09:30.
anya: Follow-ups: eli to file a kernel-usage action item (look at scratch allocation), sara to add runtime fallback + routing rule, max to prepare a small postmortem and rollback plan if the soft-evict bump causes latency regressions.
eli: Filed perf issue: https://redwood-internal/eng/issues/ENG-5123 (kernel scratch reduction + reclaim path). I included heap profiles and kv-dump.
sara: Quick patch (runtime flag) I plan to land today (small, feature-flagged). Patch summary:
```
runtime_flags:
  kv_oom_fallback: true
  longctx_prefix_eviction_threshold: 0.6
  isolate_longctx_workers: true
```
max: Good. Also adding a metric: kv_alloc_failures per pool so we can alert before OOMs.
anya: Note for postmortem: include investigation into cache reuse heuristics — kv_reuse_try() often fails because slabs get split into awkward sizes; consider merging small free ranges more eagerly.
eli: Agreed. I also want to investigate whether we can keep a small configurable ring-buffer of recently freed slabs to avoid immediate heap churn.
sara: I'll land the runtime flag behind a feature flag and schedule a canary today at 14:00 UTC. If we see elevated latency, rollback to previous eviction threshold.
anya: Thanks all. Leaving the thread open for updates; next update after canary at 14:15.
